KV2 Audio improves intelligibility at University of Bradford

By AV Magazine in Audio, Education, UK&I September 10, 2026 0

Listen to audio version of this article
Sponsored by
0:00 / 101:11
Instaread

A 20-speaker system provides even coverage from the stage to the balcony at the university’s 900-capacity Great Hall which is used for graduation ceremonies, lectures and external events.

An KV2 Audio sound system brought a new level of clarity to this summer’s graduation ceremonies at the University of Bradford’s Great Hall.

The 900-capacity venue is also used for lectures and events by external organisations, but the previous system was failing to deliver intelligibility and even coverage from the front of the stage to the balcony.

On a visit to ISE in Barcelona, the university’s AV architect Nick Cragg and his colleague Jonathan Marsden  stumbled upon a KV2 demo. “We had been searching for powerful sound suitable for both speech and media playback – and KV2 offered exactly that.”

Comprising 20 speakers, the Great Hall system was installed by the university’s AV partner and contractor, Roche AV Pro.

At its heart are two ESR106 three-way column arrays, designed for precise vocal and music reproduction in acoustically challenging environments. Concealed below the stage are four high-output ES1.8 subwoofers to reinforce low-frequency reproduction.

Two centrally flown ESD12 two-way loudspeakers provide additional coverage to the floor and balcony. The first supports the lower auditorium from front to back, while the second reinforces the upper balcony.

“The balcony was losing a lot of bass with the previous system, so the ESD12s give us the power needed to extend low-end coverage up to this area,” says Cragg.

Beneath the balcony, four ESD25 passive systems act as delays to ensure balanced audio for the tiered seating at the back. Two ESD36 passive loudspeaker units deployed to the left and right of the balcony complement the spoken word and music reproduction from the ESR106 mains.

Finally, four ultra-compact CS6 passive loudspeakers were flexibly installed along the front of the stage as infills. Firing in the opposite direction, towards the stage, are two ESD36 loudspeakers for fold-back, allowing the performers to be part of the audio experience.

“The KV2 system offers enormous potential and flexibility for a range of events,” says Cragg. “We recently ran the first graduation ceremony using the system and the improvement in vocal intelligibility was remarkable.”
